scenes.title: First, find the fragment.
scenes.caption: The camera detects a piece and separates its visible outline from the belt.
scenes.note: An outline describes appearance. It does not reveal composition.

scenes.title: Give it a temporary identity.
scenes.caption: Software calls this fragment “42” and links its observations as it travels.
scenes.note: 42 is a temporary ID for this tracked piece—not a physical tag or proof of correct matching.

scenes.title: Add geometry, if depth is available.
scenes.caption: Optional depth sensing could estimate surface height and pose to help account for distance and orientation.
scenes.note: Proposed, unselected sensor. Surface geometry is not hidden-metal depth or automatic calibration.

scenes.title: Predict when 42 reaches each station.
scenes.caption: An encoder measures belt travel. Software predicts station arrival.
scenes.note: A prediction still needs an association check: pieces can slip, overlap or rotate.

scenes.title: A changing magnetic field induces currents.
scenes.caption: AC in the coil creates a changing magnetic field. It induces closed current loops inside conducting scrap.
scenes.note: No current jumps from a coil or cover into scrap. A nonconductive sensing window is not metal shielding.

scenes.title: Measure the electrical response.
scenes.caption: The fragment’s secondary field changes receive-coil voltage. Timing and tracking would associate a reading with piece 42.
scenes.note: Amplitude and phase are relative to the drive. Calibration would use known samples; no measurements are shown.

scenes.title: Try another field direction.
scenes.caption: For this assumed patch, the transverse magnetic field crosses its face more directly. The response could be stronger.
scenes.note: Fixed pose; conceptual cutaway, not an interior scan. Actual response depends on transmitter and receiver geometry.

scenes.title: Combine observations. Keep uncertainty.
scenes.caption: Camera appearance, optional surface geometry and directional responses would inform a routing class and uncertainty.
scenes.note: Copper and aluminium both conduct. Pose and distance change response; stronger does not mean more copper.

scenes.title: Send a decision to the existing sorter.
scenes.caption: The host receives a proposed route—or recheck—with the piece ID and timing information.
scenes.note: The host actuator, collection and recovery must be tested. This is an unvalidated concept.

scope: Original illustrative schematic. No field solution, measured data, physical validation or selected electrical specifications.
